title: CSS Foundations
subtitle: Style real web pages and build responsive layouts you can see live
intendedFor: Absolute beginners who know basic HTML, students continuing from HTML Foundations, and learners preparing for JavaScript or frontend development.

courseOverview.recommendedSequence: Complete modules in order. Every technical topic connects CSS source to a visible browser-preview change.
courseOverview.summary: A practical beginner CSS course covering the cascade, selectors, typography, the box model, Flexbox, Grid, responsive design, reusable CSS, accessible states, and a complete multi-page responsive capstone.

moduleSummary.title: First Styles and the Cascade
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Connect CSS to HTML and reason about selectors, declarations, inheritance, and the cascade.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Style a semantic profile page with readable typography, color, and predictable rule precedence.

moduleSummary.title: The Box Model and Spacing
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Control element dimensions and spacing with the box model.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Create consistent content surfaces using spacing, sizing, borders, and display behavior.

moduleSummary.title: Flexbox Layout
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Build adaptable one-dimensional layouts with Flexbox.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Create flexible navigation, headers, and content rows that align and wrap cleanly.

moduleSummary.title: Grid and Responsive Design
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Build fluid two-dimensional layouts and adapt them with mobile-first responsive rules.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Create a responsive project gallery using Grid, fluid tracks, and media queries.

moduleSummary.title: Polish, Reuse, and Accessible Styling
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Turn one-off styling into reusable, maintainable CSS with accessible interaction states.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Build a consistent visual system with custom properties, reusable classes, and visible focus styles.

moduleSummary.title: Final Capstone: Responsive Personal Website
moduleSummary.coreSkill: Combine the complete CSS Foundations skill set on a real multi-page portfolio.
moduleSummary.outputFocus: Deliver one polished responsive site with reusable CSS and accessible interaction states.

authoringGuidance: This course uses profileId web, workspaceProfileId browser-web-runner, and workspacePolicyId css-browser-workspace.
Hands-on CSS tasks use kind code_input, fixedLanguage web, recipeType source_checks, semantic HTML starter files, and styles.css.
Every code_input must include explicit sourceChecks and must not include stdout tests.
Prefer source_regex checks that allow harmless whitespace and declaration-order differences.
The live browser preview is the visual feedback surface; do not tell learners to open a terminal or run Judge0.
Keep CSS Foundations JavaScript-free and framework-free. Bootstrap, Tailwind, preprocessors, package installation, and backend tooling are outside this course.
Use semantic HTML starters so the learner's primary task remains CSS.
Teach keyboard focus and readable contrast as normal styling practice.
Topic and section counts are pedagogy-driven; do not add filler content to satisfy numeric targets.

assessmentAndDelivery.suggestedBeginnerRhythm: One module per week or two short topics per study session.
assessmentAndDelivery.closingNote: Learners finish able to style responsive, maintainable, accessible web pages and are ready to add JavaScript interactivity.

modules.title: First Styles and the Cascade
modules.purpose: Build confidence with first CSS rules and understand why the browser applies one style instead of another.
learningObjectives: Compare inline, internal, and external CSS, then use external stylesheets for reusable presentation.
Write clear selectors and declaration blocks.
Use color and typography to create visual hierarchy.
Reason about the cascade, inheritance, and specificity.
guidedExercises: Edit styles.css beside provided semantic HTML.
Observe the browser preview after each meaningful style change.
Use Check Answer to validate required CSS source patterns.
Start with a one-off inline style in index.html.
Refactor the same visual rule into a <style> block for one-page organization.
Move the same rule into styles.css and link it from semantic HTML.
From later lessons onward, work primarily in styles.css while editing HTML only when selectors or linking require markup.
Reuse the completed HTML Foundations Jordan Lee portfolio instead of rebuilding HTML.
Keep index.html, about.html, contact.html, projects/portfolio.html, and images/profile.png throughout CSS Foundations.
Carry the cumulative styles.css forward from one CSS topic and module project to the next.
modules.moduleProject: Style the inherited multi-file Jordan Lee HTML Foundations portfolio with one cumulative styles.css, preserving the HTML content and image except for tiny selector/link hooks explicitly required by CSS tasks.

sections.title: First Styles and the Cascade
sections.summary: Learn the core CSS ideas for connecting, targeting, and styling a page.

topics.title: Connecting CSS to HTML
topics.summary: Apply CSS inline, with an internal <style> block, and with an external stylesheet; compare what each method solves and when external CSS becomes cleaner.
learningGoals: Apply a one-off inline style with the HTML style attribute.
Move page-level rules into an internal <style> element.
Link styles.css as an external stylesheet and explain why reusable CSS scales better.
Choose between inline, internal, and external CSS based on scope and maintainability.

topics.title: Selectors, Declarations, and Rules
topics.summary: Target elements and write CSS rules using selectors, properties, values, and declaration blocks.
learningGoals: Write type, class, and simple descendant selectors.
Build valid declaration blocks with properties and values.

topics.title: Color, Backgrounds, and Typography
topics.summary: Create visual hierarchy with readable color choices, backgrounds, font properties, and text spacing.
learningGoals: Apply foreground and background colors intentionally.
Control font family, size, weight, line height, and text alignment.

topics.title: Cascade, Inheritance, and Specificity
topics.summary: Predict which CSS declaration wins and avoid unnecessary selector conflicts.
learningGoals: Explain how source order, inheritance, and specificity affect computed styles.
Resolve simple styling conflicts without over-specific selectors.

modules.title: The Box Model and Spacing
modules.purpose: Make page structure visually understandable through predictable sizing, spacing, and box behavior.
learningObjectives: Explain and manipulate content, padding, border, and margin on the inherited portfolio.
Use spacing and borders to improve grouping without rebuilding HTML.
Use border-box, width, max-width, and image constraints to make sizing predictable.
Use display and overflow to improve existing navigation, tables, forms, and images.
guidedExercises: Continue from the exact final Module 1 six-file portfolio checkpoint.
Add padding, borders, and margin to existing semantic elements.
Keep the inherited profile image and make it fit its container safely.
Use display and overflow only to solve concrete box behavior.
Do not introduce Flexbox or Grid in Module 2.
modules.moduleProject: Turn the existing multi-page portfolio into a clearer card-based interface using only box-model, sizing, display, and overflow skills. The final styles.css becomes Module 3's checkpoint.

sections.title: The Box Model and Spacing
sections.summary: Control the boxes, dimensions, and spacing that shape page content.

topics.title: The CSS Box Model
topics.summary: Use the inherited portfolio to see how content, padding, border, and margin create the space every element occupies.
learningGoals: Identify content, padding, border, and margin as the four box-model layers.
Use padding to create space inside an element.
Use borders to reveal an element's edge.
Use margin to create space outside an element.

topics.title: Margin, Padding, and Borders
topics.summary: Refine spacing and visible edges across the same portfolio without changing its HTML content.
learningGoals: Choose margin for outside spacing and padding for inside spacing.
Use directional spacing properties intentionally.
Build borders from width, style, and color.
Apply spacing consistently to repeated site elements.

topics.title: Sizing and box-sizing
topics.summary: Control how the inherited portfolio's boxes measure width and keep images from overflowing their pages.
learningGoals: Explain the difference between content-box and border-box sizing.
Use border-box to make declared sizes easier to reason about.
Constrain images with max-width and automatic height.
Use width and max-width together for readable page sizing.

topics.title: Display and Overflow
topics.summary: Control how existing portfolio boxes participate in normal flow and handle content that is wider than its container.
learningGoals: Distinguish common block and inline behavior.
Use inline-block when an inline element needs box-like spacing.
Use overflow-x to preserve wide content without breaking the page.
Use display changes only when they solve a concrete layout behavior.

modules.title: Flexbox Layout
modules.purpose: Build one-dimensional layouts that align, distribute, and wrap content cleanly.
learningObjectives: Create Flexbox containers from existing semantic portfolio regions.
Reason about main and cross axes from flex-direction.
Align and distribute items with justify-content, align-items, and gap.
Use wrapping and flexible bases for navigation and content cards.
guidedExercises: Start from the exact locked Module 2 six-file portfolio checkpoint.
Work in styles.css and preserve all inherited HTML and the profile image.
Use Flexbox for one-dimensional layout relationships in existing semantic regions.
Do not introduce Grid or media queries before Module 4.
modules.moduleProject: Build a flexible navigation/profile layout on the same inherited portfolio, including a flex contact form and footer. Carry the final styles.css into Module 4.

sections.title: Flexbox Layout
sections.summary: Build flexible rows, navigation, and aligned content using Flexbox.

topics.title: Flex Containers and Axes
topics.summary: Turn existing portfolio regions into Flexbox containers and reason about the main and cross axes without changing the semantic HTML.
learningGoals: Create a Flexbox formatting context.
Explain how flex-direction changes the main axis.

topics.title: Alignment, Distribution, and Gap
topics.summary: Align and distribute the portfolio's existing flex items with justify-content, align-items, and gap.
learningGoals: Use justify-content and align-items for layout alignment.
Use gap for consistent spacing between flex items.

topics.title: Wrapping, Sizing, and Flex Patterns
topics.summary: Let navigation and content cards wrap when space is limited and give repeated content flexible base sizes.
learningGoals: Use flex-wrap when items should move to additional rows.
Reason about flex grow, shrink, and basis at a beginner level.
Apply Flexbox to navigation and card-row patterns.

modules.title: Grid and Responsive Design
modules.purpose: Build two-dimensional layouts that adapt across viewport sizes without device-specific hacks.
learningObjectives: Create CSS Grid layouts with columns, rows, gap, and repeat().
Use relative units, fr, and minmax() for fluid sizing.
Apply mobile-first media queries for responsive changes.
guidedExercises: Resize the browser preview while editing Grid declarations.
Compare fixed tracks with fluid minmax-based tracks.
Use Check Answer to validate required responsive source rules.
modules.moduleProject: Project: Build a Responsive Project Gallery

sections.title: Grid and Responsive Design
sections.summary: Build fluid two-dimensional layouts and adapt them across viewport sizes.

topics.title: Grid Columns and Rows
topics.summary: Create two-dimensional layouts with explicit grid columns and rows.
learningGoals: Create a grid container.
Define columns and rows using grid-template properties.

topics.title: Grid Placement, Gap, and repeat()
topics.summary: Place content in a grid and create repeated tracks without duplicating declarations.
learningGoals: Use gap for grid spacing.
Use repeat() to express repeated tracks.
Place items in simple grid regions.

topics.title: Responsive Units, minmax(), and Fluid Tracks
topics.summary: Build layouts that adapt naturally using percentages, rem, fr, minmax(), and flexible constraints.
learningGoals: Choose relative units for responsive sizing.
Use fr and minmax() to create fluid Grid tracks.

topics.title: Media Queries and Mobile-First Design
topics.summary: Start with a usable small-screen layout and enhance it as more space becomes available.
learningGoals: Write a basic media query.
Apply mobile-first responsive changes at meaningful breakpoints.
Avoid breakpoint choices that depend on one device model.

modules.title: Polish, Reuse, and Accessible Styling
modules.purpose: Turn one-off styling into a small, consistent, maintainable visual system with accessible states.
learningObjectives: Use custom properties for reusable design values.
Create reusable classes and organize stylesheet sections clearly.
Style hover and keyboard-focus states with readable contrast.
guidedExercises: Replace repeated literal values with custom properties.
Refactor repeated rule sets into reusable classes.
Test keyboard focus visibility in the browser preview.
modules.moduleProject: Project: Build a Reusable Visual System

sections.title: Polish, Reuse, and Accessible Styling
sections.summary: Create consistent reusable styling and accessible interaction feedback.

topics.title: Custom Properties and Reusable Values
topics.summary: Define reusable design values for color, spacing, and other repeated decisions.
learningGoals: Declare and consume CSS custom properties.
Use reusable values to make visual changes consistent.

topics.title: Reusable Classes and Maintainable CSS
topics.summary: Organize CSS around reusable patterns instead of copying nearly identical rules.
learningGoals: Create reusable classes for repeated visual patterns.
Group and order stylesheet sections so future edits remain understandable.

topics.title: Hover, Focus, and Accessible States
topics.summary: Style interactive elements so mouse and keyboard users can understand their state.
learningGoals: Use pseudo-classes for hover and focus states.
Create a visible keyboard focus treatment.
Preserve readable contrast in default and interactive states.

modules.title: Final Capstone: Build a Responsive Event Website
modules.purpose: Transfer the CSS skills from the cumulative learning portfolio to a fresh multi-page project with unfamiliar content and layout requirements.
learningObjectives: Apply one consistent stylesheet across a multi-page semantic website.
Combine cascade, typography, box model, Flexbox, Grid, responsive design, and reusable CSS appropriately.
Preserve semantic HTML while improving the presentation layer.
Review accessible interaction states and responsive behavior before submission.
guidedExercises: Keep the provided semantic HTML stable and work primarily in styles.css.
Carry every CSS improvement forward through the remaining milestones.
Use the browser preview at narrow and wide viewport sizes after each major layout change.
Run cumulative source checks after each milestone.
modules.moduleProject: Build a Responsive Community Tech Festival Website

sections.title: Final Capstone
sections.summary: Style one cumulative semantic portfolio into a polished, reusable, responsive, accessible website.

topics.title: Build a Responsive Community Tech Festival Website
topics.summary: Transform a provided semantic multi-page portfolio into one polished responsive design system using a cumulative styles.css file.
learningGoals: Apply a consistent color and typography system across multiple semantic pages.
Use the box model, Flexbox, and Grid where each layout problem fits best.
Create mobile-first responsive behavior with fluid sizing and media queries.
Use reusable custom properties and classes instead of duplicated styling.
Provide visible focus states and readable contrast for interactive content.
Review the complete site in the live browser preview and pass cumulative source checks.

projectBrief.scenario: A local career-readiness mentor already has a semantic multi-page portfolio in HTML and wants it transformed into a polished responsive site that looks professional on phones and larger screens.
projectBrief.role: Beginner frontend developer responsible for the presentation layer of an existing semantic website.
projectBrief.workspace: A cumulative browser-web workspace containing the provided semantic HTML portfolio, its existing image asset, and one styles.css file. Keep the HTML content stable unless a task explicitly requires a class or stylesheet-link relationship needed for CSS.
projectBrief.deliverable: One complete responsive multi-page portfolio with consistent typography and color, deliberate spacing, Flexbox and Grid layouts, reusable CSS, mobile-first behavior, and accessible interaction states.
requirements: Focus on CSS; do not turn the capstone into an HTML-authoring exercise.
Use the provided semantic page structure and content as the starting point.
Use one cumulative styles.css file across the site.
Use the cascade intentionally and avoid unnecessary selector specificity.
Use the box model for spacing and sizing, Flexbox for one-dimensional alignment, and Grid for two-dimensional layouts.
Use mobile-first responsive rules and fluid sizing rather than device-specific breakpoints.
Use custom properties and reusable classes for repeated design decisions.
Provide visible keyboard focus and readable contrast.
Use live browser preview and source checks; do not require Judge0 or terminal execution.

stepLadder.title: Connect the Stylesheet and Establish the Visual Foundation
stepLadder.requirement: Connect styles.css across the provided pages and establish the exact base typography, colors, and page-wide defaults required by the task.

stepLadder.title: Build Consistent Spacing and Content Surfaces
stepLadder.requirement: Use the box model, max-width, spacing, borders, and reusable surface styles to organize the existing content clearly.

stepLadder.title: Lay Out Navigation and Flexible Content with Flexbox
stepLadder.requirement: Use Flexbox for the required navigation, header, and one-dimensional content relationships while preserving usable wrapping.

stepLadder.title: Build the Project Gallery with Grid
stepLadder.requirement: Use CSS Grid, gap, repeat(), and fluid tracks to organize the existing project content.

stepLadder.title: Make the Site Responsive
stepLadder.requirement: Apply mobile-first responsive sizing and media queries so the complete site works cleanly from narrow to wide viewports.

stepLadder.title: Refactor, Polish, and Validate Accessibility
stepLadder.requirement: Use custom properties and reusable classes, verify focus visibility and contrast, preview every page, and pass cumulative source checks.
